claims.statement: Candidate identity is type:target, and inserting a duplicate merges into the existing candidate.

claims.statement: Candidate growth is bounded by a candidate cap, a depth limit and a request budget.

claims.statement: Retry is bounded by exponential backoff.

interpretation.summary: Backoff applies to queued retries; the failed state bypasses it and remains claimable (defect D3).
limitations: Observed in the bundled harness: one browser profile and one simulated request log, not a production measurement.

claims.statement: A permanently failing target eventually stops consuming the request budget.

locator.value: stuck candidates at quiescence: status failed with attempts and nextAttemptAt

interpretation.summary: failed is part of the claim eligibility set with no backoff, so the target is retried indefinitely (defect D3). The absence of a terminal failure state is tested, not inferred: the harness reports failed candidates still in the pool at quiescence with their attempt counts.
limitations: The design intent and the implementation conflict; this record states the conflict and does not resolve it.
Observed in the bundled harness: one browser profile and one simulated request log, not a production measurement.

claims.statement: The configured worker pool provides the configured concurrency.

interpretation.summary: A worker exits permanently on an empty frontier and the pool is never refilled, so effective concurrency collapses toward one (defect D2).
limitations: The design intent and the implementation conflict; this record states the conflict and does not resolve it.
Observed in the bundled harness: one browser profile and one simulated request log, not a production measurement.

claims.statement: Adaptive concurrency changes the number of live workers.

interpretation.summary: The counter and its diagnostics change, but the pool is created once before it is read (defect D5). Conflicting evidence: the pool is created once (CODE-018) and the adaptive counter only changes diagnostics (CODE-029).
limitations: The design intent and the implementation conflict; this record states the conflict and does not resolve it.

claims.statement: A failed acquisition still produces an observation.

interpretation.summary: Timeout, transport error and HTTP error all yield observation records with distinct statuses. test_state UNTESTED: the failure paths create observations in code (CODE-004, CODE-013, CODE-019), but no executed check asserts the resulting observation.

claims.statement: Cancelling a scan aborts in-flight requests.

interpretation.summary: stop() sets a flag; in-flight requests continue, and runtime-owned cancellation exists only in the DESIGNED v0.10. Conflicting evidence: stop() only sets a flag (CODE-018) and no request is aborted (CODE-010). DIRECT evidence: the code itself shows that only a flag is set (CODE-018) and no in-flight request is aborted (CODE-010); the design prose is context, not the ground of the finding.
limitations: The design intent and the implementation conflict; this record states the conflict and does not resolve it.

changes.description: Separate the implementation, the design series and the conversation from one transcript.
Rewrite the README against verified behaviour.
One canonical owner per concept; remove duplicate explanations.
Move the design series into a labelled roadmap document.
Archive the transcripts with a non-normative index.
Separate claim atomicity (verified) from the end-to-end ownership invariant (violated).
Document exact provider matching rules, body sniffing and provider double-match.
Remove the implied candidates() provider method; expansion is engine-owned.
Add the glossary with canonical definitions and the conflict table.
Add the verification tooling (verify, checks, simulate).
Add the scope document and mechanical non-goal enforcement.
Add the evidence register and the change register.
Archive the planning transcript so its non-normative status is explicit.
Replace collapsed status words with the canonical typed state model.
Record the scope boundary, ownership roles and the authorization contract.
Refuse re-queueing of candidates in any non-terminal state, or model re-proposed work as work.
Bind the per-URL acquisition guard to the ownership transition.
Give the failed state terminal or backoff-gated semantics.
Keep workers alive until a scan-level stop condition, or respawn them on new work.
Add a pass/fail regression gate for the single-owner invariant.
Introduce explicit scan states (idle, running, quiescent, exhausted, stopped).
Deduplicate discovery records or store corroboration as provenance.
Consult the content fingerprint index or remove it.
Maintain or remove the never-incremented acquired counter.
Drive the worker pool from the adaptive counter, or delete the feature.
Introduce an acquisition-provider boundary.
Define and persist a scan-level termination evaluator.

execution.notes: Timestamps are recorded at date granularity: the work was performed in one session on that date and per-operation wall-clock times were not captured. Mutating operations are listed per change; the earlier commits 400810d, b6dc164, e8b9aec, f4ca0e6, d6c381d, b5a1d11, 8040bba and 737c127 published this change set incrementally, and the commit carrying this record is the publication operation. The publication operations are recorded as SUCCEEDED on the same grounds as the change they publish: this record is carried by that commit, so the assertion is true for any reader who can read it. governance.notes: Three canonical grants, all capability-restricted. Content: profile DOC_REFACTOR, mutating capabilities RESTRICTED with explicit path constraints, CAP-DOCUMENT-DELETE denied. Publication: profile PUSH, five capabilities enabled and every content capability that PUSH inherits denied. Extraction (disclosed, not convenient): profile CODE_REFACTOR restricted to CAP-SOURCE-CREATE for change R-001 only, because the extraction created prototype/generic-discovery-engine.user.js and that operation must be represented rather than left uncovered; the capability to modify, rename, move or delete source was never granted, and the artifact digest is unchanged since extraction. No grant authorizes any further work.
